messages.subject: Pystan: evaluate likelihood of model
parts:
Hi

I would like to evaluate the log-posterior of a stan model for a particular setting of parameters/observations. Is there a direct API to do this? If not, it would be nice to have it. I currently do a hack where I just run an optimiser that converges immediately and use the value from there, but it's kind of dirty.

Thanks!
Heiko

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pystan: evaluate likelihood of model
parts:
1. Yes, you can get the density function and evaluate it
at different parameter values in PyStan --- I don't know the
call, but the functionality's there.

2. No, you can't change out the data easily. The data is
written into constant variables in the constructor of a model's
class. But what you can do is write something in generated
quantities to evaluate predictions on new data given the
parameters. That way, you automatically get full Bayes on
the predictive inferences.

- Bob

It is confusing! You do need to instantiate the model as Stan cannot do
much without the compiled model. You can, however, just call the
constructor, StanModel, and then use log_prob. No need to call sampling.

Best,

Allen
